items.stem: During nutrition assessment, which step best supports an accurate nutrition diagnosis?

options.text: Integrating anthropometric, biochemical, clinical and dietary data together
options.rationale: Correct: a nutrition diagnosis draws on multiple data domains, not one value alone.

options.text: Relying solely on body mass index
options.rationale: A single value cannot establish a nutrition diagnosis on its own.

options.text: Using the patient's self-reported goal weight only
options.rationale: A goal weight is not assessment data for a diagnosis.
Dietary intake is essential assessment data.

items.explanation: Correct: a nutrition diagnosis draws on multiple data domains, not one value alone.

items.stem: A patient with advancing chronic kidney disease (not yet on dialysis) typically needs which dietary adjustment?

options.text: Controlled protein intake appropriate to the stage
options.rationale: Correct: protein is managed to the disease stage in pre-dialysis CKD to limit uraemic burden.
Unrestricted protein is generally not appropriate in pre-dialysis CKD.
Carbohydrate elimination is not the standard CKD modification.
Potassium often needs limiting, not maximising, as CKD advances.

items.stem: Which TWO are critical control points in preventing foodborne illness in a foodservice operation?

options.text: Holding hot foods at or above the required temperature
options.rationale: Correct: temperature control during holding is a critical control point.

options.text: Cooking foods to the required internal temperature
options.rationale: Correct: cooking to the specified internal temperature is a critical control point.

options.text: Choosing the colour of serving trays
options.rationale: Tray colour has no food-safety role.

options.text: Printing the menu in two fonts
options.rationale: Menu formatting is unrelated to food safety.
Ambience does not control foodborne hazards.

items.explanation: Correct: temperature control during holding is a critical control point.
